The book preserves the central category of alignment with God but narrows the extension by making lived obedience the direct definition rather than a subsequent fruit of imputed standing.",
  "extension_reasoning": "The book adds the explicit definition of righteousness as commandment-obedience and the opposite of sin, while the common-view note acknowledges the consensus's imputed-forensic emphasis but subordinates it to right-living as primary. This refines the boundary by prioritizing ethical conduct over forensic declaration as the core meaning, without replacing the referent.",

The book's entry defines righteousness as right-living—God's commandments lived out—with God Himself defined as Right-Living by nature. This directly aligns with the consensus core of conformity to God's character and standard, while the common-view note explicitly contrasts the book's framing against the imputed-forensic emphasis that dominates much of the listed responses. The scriptures cited reinforce both standing and obedience, but the book's own wording elevates lived obedience as the primary identification.

I classify this as REFINED: the core referent remains the same (alignment with God), but the book narrows the extension by making commandment-obedience the direct definition rather than a fruit of standing, and it adds the opposite of sin as a boundary marker. The printed citations provide strong support because they include both the imputation passages (Romans 4, Philippians 3) and the obedience passages (Deuteronomy 6:25, Psalm 119:172, 1 John 3:7) that the book draws upon.

This is not DIVER GENT because the standing and living are causally related (fruit), and the book does not deny their connection—it subordinates the former to the latter. It is not MATCH because the book's explicit contrast with the common imputed view creates a material boundary shift.
